item.title: We’ve got a loaner gun if you’d like?
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: What a difference 40 miles make. After leaving Bessie parked in the Pacific Beach neighbourhood of San Diego with the doors unlocked for weeks, I departed north for Newport Beach with a pit stop for a tune up at Gary’s RV in Oceanside. It’s the classic case where someone who knows their blood pressure is [...]
item.content:encoded:
What a difference 40 miles make.  After leaving Bessie parked in the Pacific Beach neighbourhood of San Diego with the doors unlocked for weeks, I departed north for Newport Beach with a pit stop for a tune up at Gary’s RV in Oceanside.  It’s the classic case where someone who knows their blood pressure is giving them dizzy spells will postpone going to the doctor because they can still walk and breathe.  Such is the case with an RV I have driven all the way from Canada to the Mexican border the entire time unable to cut the engine while in Park due to it continuing to fire and shoot black smoke everywhere.

Bessie's equivalent of triple bypass surgery

To hear that the carburetor was “completely fucked” (Gary’s words, not mine) was no surprise, nor the fact I’d have to sleep in the parking lot overnight.  The idea of that seemed downright comforting after a friend I met in San Diego who goes by the name “Crazy Scott” decided to stop by Bessie my last night sometime around 11 PM with a flashlight, while banging on the doors and windows yelling “this is the SDPD, open up!”  I thought it was quite smart of me to hide under the covers and pretend the RV was uninhabited…well, I still think that was a good choice after hearing the neighbours on the street the night earlier proclaiming during one of my late night techno parties “not only does he keep parking here, but he has to rub it in our face!”

Every mechanic I’ve met so far is somehow amazed that Bessie’s held together as well as she has, and Gary could tell from the seals that my carburetor had never been rebuilt, and he swore he’d never seen one last more than a dozen years.  So out it goes, gets soaked in some solvent overnight, gets some new gaskets and fittings in the morning, and $10 says I’ll make the $400 back on fuel economy alone by the time my trip is done.  Well, I’m actually working on a sales pitch for Gary to see if he’d like his store ranked #1 in Google, but he already told me he “fucking hates computers” so it might be a tough sell.

Having been told the shop closed at 5 PM sharp, I returned at 4:45 to get the keys to the overnight gate to find Gary and a friend of his in the office watching some DVD on Fords of the Fifties.  I was immediately pushed out a chair, given a Diet Pepsi and invited to join what they lovingly referred to as “car porn”.  After deciphering that I was over 21, Gary offered me some of the whiskey he and his friend were drinking, before his friend shouted “no, there’s not enough!” and poured himself another two finger glass.

After finishing the movie over an hour later and learning a great deal about overhead valves, big blocks, that the grill on an Edsel “looks like a vagina” and that mechanics over the age of 50 are all generally great guys because they love what they do so much, I told Gary I was going to go back up towards Grubby’s where he’d pointed me for lunch earlier.

“Kid, I wouldn’t head up that direction, Oceanside’s a different place at night.”

Seeing the quizzical look on my face, mainly because Grubby’s was under 2 blocks away and I would be sleeping here, he offered me a bit of American reassurance.

“We’ve got a loaner gun if you’d like?”

item.title: Wide Angle Madness
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: So I’ve been holding out on all my good content pretending I’m too busy. Well, I actually am too busy, but never too busy to take some more dope photos. I was lucky enough at Christmas this year to get a Sigma 8-16 lens for my Canon T2i, and while I’ve had limited time to [...]
item.content:encoded:
So I’ve been holding out on all my good content pretending I’m too busy.  Well, I actually am too busy, but never too busy to take some more dope photos.

Back to my old HDR tricks

I was lucky enough at Christmas this year to get a Sigma 8-16 lens for my Canon T2i, and while I’ve had limited time to test it out, so far the results are absolutely outstanding.  One of these “side projects” I keep talking about is actually a site dedicated to pimping the lens where I can have my commercial slant but still stay true to my passions of photography without completely selling out.  It’s not ready yet which is why I was holding off on letting the cat out of the bag, but I have enough sample shots now there’s no point depriving everyone.  Plus, I can always edit this post, make a few more and self-promote and backlink the sh!t out of myself…but that’s another story for another day.

In the meantime, these shots were all taken within a 20 minute walk of where I’m staying in beautiful Pacific Beach in San Diego California.  It’s been 70 degrees F and sunny for a few weeks now, and I’m obviously not too disappointed about my plan for the last 8 or so months to “winter” here, as I believe the photos will illustrate.

Perhaps more the subject than the shot

Some of you may have had a chance to check out my Canon extension tube work in a post last week, this one is just another trick in the lens bag.  Almost every shot from my trip to date was taken with my Sigma 30mm prime lens, but now that I’ve got the wide angle, it opens up a whole new world.  Without getting overly technical, 30mm versus 8mm means I can fit 375% more subject in each frame.  While it seems like this would be best for landscape photography, I’m finding it’s actually best for capturing and amplifying a subject in the foreground pitted against an expansive background.  But, I haven’t had enough chance to test out all the possible combinations, so once I get back on the road again on Thursday, the experimentation across America should commence once again.

In the meantime, check the gallery.

item.title: Album of the Week: Kick by INXS
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: If you don’t recognize at least four of the tracks off this album as instant classics, where have you been the last 25 years? And if it’s so damn popular, why exactly am I “reviewing” it? For starters, if you haven’t popped INXS in the deck lately, you’re missing out and you’ll immediately be reminded [...]
item.content:encoded:
If you don’t recognize at least four of the tracks off this album as instant classics, where have you been the last 25 years?  And if it’s so damn popular, why exactly am I “reviewing” it?  For starters, if you haven’t popped INXS in the deck lately, you’re missing out and you’ll immediately be reminded why.  And secondly, for the first time in six months I’m actually busy enough to not have time to make posts, so I had to do something.  Without XSively blurring the lines between damn fine 80s power pop and my personal woes launching other websites while trying to legally remain in the US (perhaps those should be the next post), let’s jump into it.

After having the incredibly polished, infectious sound of the songs off Kick burned into my memory since childhood, I was surprised to learn that INXS actually spent almost 10 years toiling as an Australian bar band before they made it big.  And also foregoing my usual studiousness, I haven’t listened to any of their earlier stuff.  But why bother, because Kick is it.  Essentially the pinnacle of 80s popular music, fusing the braddicio of the long-haired, sly but tortured lead singer with clean electric rock guitar and crisp to the point of being overproduced repetitive drum rhythms, INXS is almost post-new wave.  Whatever it is, it just works, and not just judging from the worldwide multi-platinum status.

Arguably the most recognizable song on the album is the second track New Sensation, which was actually the third single, so for it to make it through a quarter century of radio play is what I would call longevity.  Amazingly enough, it could just as easily be heard on the classic rock station versus the light adult contemporary, mainly because it’s that good.  The same goes for most of the singles, there’s a general musical catchiness that’s brought to the forefront by the production that’s hard for anyone to argue with.  Yet the instrumentation is stripped down and funky and there’s something concealed and nasty about Michael Hutchence’s whispered yet forceful lyrics.

This is none the more evident on my favourite track of the lot Need You Tonight.  While I have yet to try, I dare any guy to recite the opening few lyrics to a girl at the bar as a pickup line and see if it doesn’t get you to second base.  “All we’ve got is this moment, the 21st century’s yesterday, you can care all you want…” OK, we’re off to a good start, how about “so slide over here and give me a moment, your moves are so raw I’ve got to let you know…” then maybe finish off with  “there’s something about you girl, that makes me sweat.” Lost in all of this energy is the fact that there are at least four different funky and utterly catchy pieces of the riff interplaying with each other in the background, most importantly the famous jangling guitar stab.  And then part way through the song Michael Hutchence starts yelling “I’M LONELY!!” as the new refrain.  But wait, you set the whole song up on your indestructible coolness?  I guess internationally renowned rock stars are people too!

Wow, I’m going to a review an entire record only mentioning the three most famous songs.  And I didn’t even touch on Devil Inside yet!  Another murderously slick riff…bah-bah-badda-dah-dada-dada…it gets stuck in your head as much as any of the other tracks.  Couple that with the fact that all the rest of the songs have their own unique and fun feel makes for an amazing cohesive album that was at the forefront of musical trends when it came out and still holds to this day.

You can pick this album up at Amazon

Or iTunes

item.title: Popular Science: Maybe Magazines Aren’t Dead After All
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Having not read a real magazine in perhaps years, I was genuinely impressed flipping through this month’s issue of Popular Science as I actually learned several things, so I thought I’d share some of them: Genetically Modified Mosquitoes I had no idea that these had been introduced to the Cayman Islands and succeeded in reducing [...]
item.content:encoded:
Having not read a real magazine in perhaps years, I was genuinely impressed flipping through this month’s issue of Popular Science as I actually learned several things, so I thought I’d share some of them:

Genetically Modified Mosquitoes

I had no idea that these had been introduced to the Cayman Islands and succeeded in reducing the mosquito population by 80% to fight dengue fever.  Who knows what the consequences are down the road for whatever used to eat them, but who doesn’t hate mosquitoes, so hooray!

The “Internet Kill Switch” Bill

Dubbed Senate Bill 3480 “Protecting Cyberspace as a National Asset”, there’s actually legislation in place right now that would allow the government to shut down the internet “in case of emergency”.  Despite the fact this is practically impossible, the idea that they need such a thing and what the real motives are is frightening.  Isn’t that what they do in Iran and North Korea?  Worse still, it was proposed by Joe Lieberman, the same man who demanded Amazon and PayPal cut all ties with WikiLeaks arbitrarily without any sort of court injunction.  I also found a great site on the NY Times where you can track it, or any other bill’s progress through the political machine.

The Second Green Revolution

Think about this, organic farmers and genetically modified food manufacturers working together.  At first it sounds outrageous, but after awhile it’s apparent it’s the only way we can go forward.  Harvesting land in any fashion is already a disruption of the natural order of ecosystems.  As it stands, we pull oil from a hole in the ground, convert it to fertilizer, transport it great distances using more fossil fuels, then pour it back in the ground, it’s not sustainable.  We’ve been doing “genetic engineering” for thousands of years by always picking the quickest ripening fruits with the most seeds that are the most climate and disease resistant, and now we’re all techno geniuses, so why not program that into the food from the get go?  (Sorry, I can’t find the original article, but this one’s kinda neat)

The “Smart” Basketball

The incessant talk about using microchips to detect when a soccer ball or hockey puck crossed the goal line never really piqued my interest either, but this one’s kinda neat.  Put some sensors and gyroscopes inside a basketball during practice and you can scientifically tell a kid “you need 18.2% more backspin on your jump shot”.  Kinda smart, kinda too analytical, but definitely enough to make Tim Hardaway cringe.  I’m terrible at shooting, but I used to love shouting “you’re a BRICK LAYER” at other people’s missed shots in gym class.  I would have been way more in my element yelling “nice 3.7 revolutions per seconds, jerk!”

Camcorders with Built-in HDR

For those of you following some of my sillier shots where I stitch multiple exposures of images together in Photoshop to get higher dynamic range, Casio has introduced a camcorder called the TRYX that does this with every single frame on the fly!

Other Random Factoids

-the world’s largest supercomputer consumes the amount of energy equivalent to eating 50,000 BLT sandwiches daily

-speaking of supercomputers, IBM’s Watson is primed to be a competitor on Jeopardy in the natural language processing equivalent to Deep Blue versus Kasparov

-I can’t even find a link to it on the internet, but they built a do-it-yourself rice cake maker involving a blowtorch and some metal pipe, it was really quite awesome

-but of course the exact same Nissan ad was on the back of the Maxim laying on the same table, so maybe what I was saying about the relevance and importance of magazines isn’t so relevant or important after all

item.title: Canon Extension Tube
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: I’m going to let you in on a little secret about the newest toy I got for my Canon T2i camera, the macro extension tube: There’s almost no reason whatsoever to buy the actual Canon Extension Tube versus a no name brand like Kenko or Opteka! For less than the price of one Canon Extension [...]
item.content:encoded:
I’m going to let you in on a little secret about the newest toy I got for my Canon T2i camera, the macro extension tube: There’s almost no reason whatsoever to buy the actual Canon Extension Tube versus a no name brand like Kenko or Opteka! For less than the price of one Canon Extension Tube, you get a set of three different lengths that can be combined together while still maintaining the electrical connections for aperture and autofocus control, the only downside being the use of plastic in the construction.  Even better, unless you’re a professional, you can easily delay the need to get a dedicated macro lens when a set of macro extension tubes can give you about half of the same functionality at one tenth the price.

For the uninitiated, a macro extension tube is a hollow piece of metal and/or plastic that you attach to your SLR in between the lens and camera body.  This changes the focal length of the lens, so a 50mm lens with a 25 extension tube will act like a 75mm lens in terms of magnification, but with two major differences.  The first is that it will no longer be able to focus to infinity and depending on the tube/lens focal length combo may only be able to focus feet or inches away.  Secondly, your minimum focusing distance will also decrease.

On my Sigma 30 lens where I usually need to be a foot away from something, I can lessen this to a matter of inches with a 12 extension tube.  While this isn’t useful for birds or bugs, for plants, found objects and textures, the results can be outstanding, especially if you’re just starting out and wanting to play around.  I’d almost want to call it “hackro” to coin a new term, but as soon as you start hitting magnification factors higher than 1:1, you’ve achieved the textbook definition of macro.

I purchased a set of 13mm, 21mm and 31mm Opteka extension tubes for $80 and haven’t looked back since.  They also come rebranded as CowboyStudio, but are the exact same as Opteka.  I even went to several of the local camera stores in San Diego which sold the Kenko extension tubes and found them to be almost identical, but costing over twice the price.  And worse still are the Canon Extension Tubes which would run at over $200 for just a 12mm and a 25mm.

I’ve started a gallery page of macro sample shots achieved with the extension tubes that I’ll be expanding on over time, but even the classic example of the penny turns out pretty well using the 18-55 kit lens.  Sure, the sharpness and contrast aren’t out of this world due to the lens (especially noticeable on the 2nd and 3rd oranges below) but it’s an incredible amount of fun and impressive to me nonetheless as all of a sudden I have a camera that’s also a magnifying glass.

The only other drawback to the extension tube approach is when you have to get that close to the subject, the depth of field is incredibly short.  This can still be compensated for with aperture, but only so much.  You can sometimes use this to your advantage to achieve interesting effects like the hibiscus blossom below, and in a future post I’ll outline another trick of depth of field blending using Photoshop and a tripod taking multiple pictures.

Just to summarize why I feel a Canon Extension Tube (or ever better the generic version from Opteka) is a great investment and addition to any of the lenses in your bag, here’s a quick bullet list of the pros and cons.

Benefits

  • increased magnification
  • lower minimum focusing distance (MFD)
  • maintain electrical connection for aperture and autofocus control
  • works with EF-S lenses

Drawbacks

  • heavy lenses (i.e. glass telephoto over 300mm) might stress the camera body and tubes
  • the longer the lens focal length, the less the magnification increase
  • depth of field is limited (but this is often part of macro photography)

item.title: Trader Joe’s and Drive-Thru Banking
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Those two concepts are as foreign to me as the fact I can wake up at 9 AM and walk on the beach in shorts because it’s already 70 degrees outside. That’s not supposed to happen in January, but I suppose that’s why I came to San Diego. “Wintering” here is the term I use, [...]
item.content:encoded:
Those two concepts are as foreign to me as the fact I can wake up at 9 AM and walk on the beach in shorts because it’s already 70 degrees outside.  That’s not supposed to happen in January, but I suppose that’s why I came to San Diego.  “Wintering” here is the term I use, except it feels like summer, so mission accomplished.  Wondering if anyone even works in this town when there are hundreds of surfers on Pacific Beach, I learn today is a holiday.  God bless Martin Luther King, and contrary to popular belief I do actually keep track of what day it is to stay in synch with everyone else, otherwise I would miss my chance to make some money at poker night.  It’s Monday, so there.

I need a haircut?

For anyone following along since Vancouver to remember the junk I wrote about self-actualization, it’s actually happening.  I had a plan to get to San Diego by 2011 treating everything as a vacation, then refocusing to figure out how to make internet monies and keep the Blimpy train going forever.  It’s a long, slow process and the main thing I’ve learned from the internet marketing course I’m taking online is if I sell my soul and make a few hundred websites like BuyAniPadRightNow.net, that would probably work.  Unfortunately, I still have a soul, perhaps spending more time in America will slowly cure me of that and I can hire someone in the Philippines to write the blog for me or program a bot to steal posts from elsewhere.

The real problem right now is figuring out how to extend my stay in the US legally, the biggest deterrent likely being the fact I have no intention of getting a haircut.  Or that I had to change the pic slider on the main blimpyb.com page as the old one is no longer free because whoever wrote it wants his internet monies too.  Writing one line of PHP code took me two hours to get it working correctly, this is the most “work” I have done in six months.  And it still ain’t quite right, watch me waste an entire day over nothing.

But that’s all just noise.  I really am just rebuilding my strength before I head back up to Orange Country, then Palm Springs, then Joshua Tree National Park, then Spring Training baseball, then getting a press pass for the pits at a NASCAR race, then Vegas…the ridicu-list goes on.

item.title: Album of the Week: Blitz ‘n’ Ass by Jahcoozi
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Having rekindled my electronic roots last week with Supermodified, I realized I should maybe dwell on my bread and butter a tad longer. This time around we’ll be looking at German glitch hop/dancehall trio Jahcoozi’s second album Blitz ‘n’ Ass. Funnily enough, this album has two characteristics I usually find quite off-putting. The first is [...]
item.content:encoded:
Having rekindled my electronic roots last week with Supermodified, I realized I should maybe dwell on my bread and butter a tad longer.  This time around we’ll be looking at German glitch hop/dancehall trio Jahcoozi’s second album Blitz ‘n’ Ass.

Funnily enough, this album has two characteristics I usually find quite off-putting.  The first is the almost blatant style biting from MIA.  As soon as the vocals drop on the opener BLN you’ll notice the similarity; Jahcoozi’s MC Sasha Perera has the exact same born in Sri Lanka, raised in Britain pedigree as Maya Arulpragasam.  Not only that, but her sly yet erratic delivery is belted over bombastic, heavily synthesized beats, again all too familiar.  However, despite the perceived sameness with MIA, I’m more than willing to let Jahcoozi slide because to my ears it’s ultimately a different sound after repeated listens.  The music isn’t nearly as cluttered and comes across with exceptional clarity and punch.  As for the lyrics, there’s a much greater emphasis on fun and sexuality, and while it is political, there’s none of the misguided, pseudo BS kind that ultimately caused me to completely disregard MIA as an artist, despite how much I enjoyed Piracy Funds Terrorism and Arular back in the day.  Jahcoozi isn’t interested in generating controversy for its own sake to build hype, they just want to make hard hitting electronic music.

My second gripe with this album is that it takes awhile to catch its stride with the second half being much stronger, and even then a few of the tracks are forgettable.  The opener BLN has jump and is catchy, but sounds like something I could have heard years ago, making it good but not great.  However, by the time the third track Gameboy gets rolling, its underwater thump, handclap syncopation and use of vocals as a melodic and percussive instrument to tie everything together has me hooked.  There’s even a simple message about kids these days sitting on the couch playing video games rather than going outside and playing with real people, but it’s nothing more than cute while letting the music speak for itself, which I greatly appreciate over MIA’s thinly veiled call to impeach all the world’s politicians while supporting the Tamil Tigers.  Not that there’s anything wrong with either of those goals, until they’re used to sell records.

By the time the record reaches my favourite cut Takin’ Your Street, I’m also reminded why I don’t recommend electronic albums all that often: you need to have a good stereo system to hear half the notes.  I can’t even imagine listening to this song on headphones as I sit here with my entire RV pulsating, jumbling my internal organs while generating strange looks from passersby on the street.  Maybe they’d understand if they hopped in to hear the full spectrum of the song’s fading in and out interplay of clicks, clangs, growls and scratches.  Or on second thought, maybe not, I woke up this morning to find a note on my windshield that someone had called the City of San Diego on me…

The album finishes with several good tracks using a bit more relaxed sound, but still maintaining the exceptionally crisp production found throughout.  All in all, while Blitz ‘n’ Ass isn’t genre defining, the standout tracks are absolutely searing electronic very useful for showing off how pimp your RV stereo system is to the point you are asked to move it, and also generally a lot of fun.  Also recommended for anyone who likes the MIA sound.


You can pick up this album at Amazon


Or iTunes

item.title: I’m Still Here
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Other than the fact I’m not a limitlessly talented actor and don’t have millions in my bank account, I’m pretty sure the biggest lacking parallel between me and Joaquin Phoenix is that I can’t grow such a natty beard. I am of course referring to the recent flash in the pan popular documentary about Phoenix’s [...]
item.content:encoded:
Other than the fact I’m not a limitlessly talented actor and don’t have millions in my bank account, I’m pretty sure the biggest lacking parallel between me and Joaquin Phoenix is that I can’t grow such a natty beard.

I am of course referring to the recent flash in the pan popular documentary about Phoenix’s supposed collapse from Johnny Cash and Gladiator Oscar nominated actor to coke snorting, hooker banging reject-all reject.  I just got the chance to finally watch I’m Still Here last week after incessantly talking it up my entire trip, and while one of the best descriptors I can think of for the movie itself is jarring, I was nonetheless thoroughly impressed.

For those of you not familiar with the story, Joaquin Phoenix decided after his 2008 movie Two Lovers with Gwyneth Paltrow that he was done with acting, wanted to pursue a career in hip hop and generally quit giving a fuck about everything, especially the Hollywood marketing machine.  Problem is, it was all an act…except it wasn’t, which is the entire brilliance of it.  And I use the term brilliance reluctantly, it was completely self-indulgent, disrespectful to a lot of people and borderline insane.  Granted, that’s exactly how I like it, but as some of my Hollywood friends pointed out, that first disaster interview he gave on Letterman may very well have cost some people their jobs.  But you can’t make an omelette without breaking a few eggs.

Letterman actually played it as well as he could have, while still remaining shallow and condescending, which are his true colours.  Joaquin’s shone through as well because when I say this was an act but not an act, whatever it was totally sabotaged his career costing him millions in the process and took more balls than any Hollywood actor you may perhaps ever see.  It’s one thing to self destruct, hell the same could be said about fattening cue card reading Marlon Brando, but at least he still played ball.  Joaquin played ball only to prove that it was all a ball game.  And by turning it into such a grandiose absurd spectacle, all the lines start to blur as the “mock” intentions led to easily foreseeable real consequences.

He and director Casey Affleck would go on to call this a commentary on the nature of media and celebrity, but to think the extrapolations end there would be foolish, and I’m living proof.  Countless times in his supposed revelationary introspective moments Phoenix repeated the following two mantras.  One, that doing what other people say, standing where they tell you and saying what they wrote is not self-expression, it’s imprisonment.  Two, that we are all embroiled in an act of trying to be perceived by others.  I used to be guilty of the first, I am still guilty of the second.

Just watch the movie.  It’s hard going, really offensive and worth it.
